article_title: Aneurin Bevan and how the Query Club set him on path to power

tasks.prompt: What central argument does the article make about the Query Club?
options: It was mainly a social club for retired mine owners.
It helped Bevan and fellow socialists learn how to gain institutional power and pursue reform.
It opposed the Tredegar Medical Aid Society's expansion.
It persuaded Bevan to leave politics for coal mining.
tasks.correct_answer: It helped Bevan and fellow socialists learn how to gain institutional power and pursue reform.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה טוענת שהמועדון לימד את בוואן וחבריו כיצד להשיג השפעה במוסדות, ודרך זו עיצבה את הקריירה הפוליטית שלו.

tasks.prompt: What was distinctive about the Query Club when it began in 1921?
options: It was a government committee based in London.
It was a semi-secret debating society formed largely by colliers in Tredegar.
It was a medical charity controlled by mine owners.
It admitted only members of Parliament.
tasks.correct_answer: It was a semi-secret debating society formed largely by colliers in Tredegar.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: המועדון החל כחברה חצי-סודית של דיון, שרוב חבריה היו כורי פחם מטרדגר.

tasks.prompt: How broad had the Tredegar Medical Aid Society become by Walter Conway's death in 1933?
options: It served only 5,000 miners.
It covered one hospital but no doctors or dentists.
It had 20,000 members, about 95% of the town, including families and non-miners.
It had been replaced by the NHS.
tasks.correct_answer: It had 20,000 members, about 95% of the town, including families and non-miners.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ב-1933 החברה מנתה 20,000 חברים, כ-95% מן העיר, וכללה גם נשים, ילדים ומי שלא היו כורים.

tasks.prompt: What does “eluding” mean in Bevan's statement that power was still eluding them?
options: Being distributed fairly among them
Being formally explained to them
Being used openly against them
Remaining beyond their reach despite their efforts
tasks.correct_answer: Remaining beyond their reach despite their efforts
tasks.explanation_hebrew: eluding מתאר דבר שחומק ואינו מושג למרות המאמצים; בוואן חש שהכוח עדיין נמצא במקום אחר.

tasks.prompt: What electoral path did Bevan follow according to the article?
options: Tredegar town council, county council, then Parliament
Hospital board, House of Lords, then town council
Parliament, county council, then the Medical Aid Society
Trade union office, Welsh government, then Parliament
tasks.correct_answer: Tredegar town council, county council, then Parliament
tasks.explanation_hebrew: המועדון הציב את בוואן למועצת העיר ב-1922; בהמשך נבחר למועצת המחוז ולבסוף לפרלמנט ב-1929.

tasks.prompt: Why did the Query Club seek seats on many local boards and committees?
options: To keep political debate away from working people
To reduce the membership of the medical society
To replace local services with private companies
To shift influence from established industrial interests toward reforms benefiting ordinary people
tasks.correct_answer: To shift influence from established industrial interests toward reforms benefiting ordinary people
tasks.explanation_hebrew: המוסדות המקומיים נשלטו בידי גורמים הקשורים לחברת הברזל והפחם; חברי המועדון ביקשו להעביר השפעה לסוציאליסטים ולקדם שינוי.

tasks.prompt: Give two ways the Query Club helped prepare Bevan for national politics.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין שתי דרכים שונות שבהן פעילות המועדון תרמה להתפתחותו הפוליטית של בוואן.
expected_points: Debates helped him develop powerful speaking and argument-deconstruction skills.
The club taught members to identify where institutional power was located.
It helped place him on Tredegar town council.
Its continuing search for power led him from local to county and then parliamentary politics.

tasks.prompt: Summarise the relationship between the Query Club, local institutions and Bevan's later career in 3–4 sentences.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לקשור בין הקמת המועדון, הכניסה למוסדות המקומיים, התפתחות בוואן והמורשת הלאומית.
expected_points: The Query Club began in 1921 as a semi-secret socialist debating group in Tredegar.
Members sought positions on councils, boards and other bodies dominated by established industrial interests.
This strategy and the club's debates shaped Bevan's pursuit of power and oratory.
Bevan later entered Parliament, founded the NHS and pursued housing reform.

tasks.prompt: How did Tredegar provide both a model and a motivation for Bevan's creation of the NHS? Use evidence from the article.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר גם את תנאי החיים וחוסר הכוח כמניע וגם את חברת הסיוע הרפואי כמודל, תוך שימוש בראיות.
expected_points: Working people produced wealth but had little control over work and living conditions.
The Medical Aid Society was funded by small wage contributions.
It expanded to cover about 95% of Tredegar and included families and non-miners.
It provided doctors, nurses, dentists and hospital care.
The article presents this universal local scheme as a foundation for the NHS.

tasks.prompt: Evaluate the statement “Power was central to the Query Club's strategy.” Write one paragraph using at least three article details.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לטעון טענה ברורה, לשלב לפחות שלוש ראיות מדויקות ולהבחין בין השגת כוח לבין מטרת הרפורמה.
expected_points: Local institutions were dominated by figures linked to the Tredegar Iron and Coal Company.
The club aimed to place like-minded socialists on every influential committee and board.
Members gained seats on the town council and other bodies during the 1920s.
Bevan moved to county politics and then Parliament because he believed decisive power lay elsewhere.
The pursuit of power was intended to improve conditions for ordinary people.
